beats.narration_en: Same swerve on a wet road. One car spins out and one doesn't.
Swerve hard and the rear tires can lose their grip first
and once the back starts to slide the car turns faster than you steer.
Steering back is often too late to catch it.
Stability control is built to catch that moment.
A sensor in the middle of the car measures how fast it is turning
and a sensor on the steering column reads where you are steering.
When the car turns faster than the steering asks for it is starting to spin
so the system brakes just one wheel on the outside front.
That one brake drags the nose back out of the spin
using the same valve block and pump as your ABS.
It all happens in a fraction of a second and the car stays pointed down the road.
So keep steering where you want to go and let it work.
